brief.outcome: Reach 100 sign-ups a month from Google organic search within six months, up from about 15, without claims about legal compliance that cannot be backed up.

ambition.goal_beyond: Google becomes a steady, predictable source of new HR-software customers that does not depend on one writer's spare hours.
rungs: Fix titles, descriptions and sign-up prompts on the 45 existing posts and publish a few new posts.
Find, from Search Console and GA4 data, which searches and pages can lead to sign-ups, then refresh, merge or write only the few pages with the most sign-up potential.
Do rung 2, then keep it true with a monthly check that flags pages losing clicks or sign-ups and picks the next three pages for the writer.
ambition.judge: Google Search Console clicks and GA4 organic sign-up events, read from Google's own reports, comparing changed pages with unchanged pages over the same weeks.

brief.deliverable: Refreshed and new posts plus title, description and sign-up prompt fixes, drafted in Webflow and published with your approval, a monthly check, and an honest readout against 100 sign-ups a month.
done: Sign-up tracking checked, and the true organic sign-up baseline stated
Every post sorted into keep, fix, refresh, merge or retire, with the numbers behind it
Chosen plan recorded, sized to the part-time writer's hours
Drafts built in Webflow with no unbacked claims, published only with your approval
Changed pages read against unchanged pages in Search Console and GA4
Monthly check set up and learnings saved

Working data stays in this project

answers.question: What does the blog bring today?
answers.answer: 45 posts, about 1,200 organic visits a month and maybe 15 sign-ups a month from organic (GA4, reported).

answers.question: Which tools can your AI reach?
answers.answer: Google Search Console and GA4 connected read-only. Webflow site with draft access via the Webflow MCP.

answers.question: What is the target?
answers.answer: 100 organic sign-ups a month within six months.

answers.question: What are the limits?
answers.answer: One part-time writer, no budget for links, no claims about legal compliance we cannot back up.

answers.question: Where should data live and who decides?
answers.answer: In this project. The head of marketing decides.

research.approach: Practitioners start from what Google already shows: the queries and pages in Search Console, with impressions, position and click-through, joined to which landing pages lead to a sign-up in GA4. They size the gap with simple arithmetic (visits needed at the current and a better sign-up rate), find pages that rank on page two or have lost clicks, and only write new posts where a topic is close to the product. Old posts are refreshed with real new content, not just a new date, and titles, descriptions and sign-up prompts are fixed first because they cost the least. Changes are published in batches and read against pages left unchanged, because search results lag by weeks.

sources.title: Performance report (Search Console Help, Google)
sources.note: Defines clicks, impressions, CTR and average position, with Queries, Pages, Devices, Search appearance and Dates as dimensions. No date on the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: About key events (Analytics Help, Google)
sources.note: An action that matters most to the business is marked as a key event so it shows in reports and explorations, including session key event rate. No date on the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content (Google Search Central)
sources.note: Self-assessment on original value, visible authorship and expertise; warns against pages made mainly for search traffic, mass-produced content and changing dates to seem fresh. No date on the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Republishing content for SEO and AI: how to update posts, not just change dates (Ahrefs)
sources.note: Find declining pages, skip ones just overhauled, check business potential and whether the problem is content or links, and measure traffic before and after. One post it refreshed gained 36% (single vendor example).

sources.title: Add SEO title and meta description (Webflow Help Center)
sources.note: Seen in search results; the page itself blocked fetching. Per the result summary: page-level SEO settings, a pattern for CMS collection pages, changes need publishing, and indexing can take days to months. No date on the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

steps.name: Set what the site may and may not claim
steps.why: The owner bans compliance claims we cannot back, so the allowed claims come first.

steps.name: Pull Search Console queries and pages, and GA4 sign-ups by landing page
steps.why: Raw query and page rows show real demand, rank and click-through; GA4 shows which pages lead to sign-ups.

steps.name: Check sign-up tracking and that posts can be found and indexed
steps.why: A wrong sign-up count or unindexed posts makes every later number misleading.

steps.name: Size the gap and sort every post
steps.why: Arithmetic on visits and sign-up rate shows whether traffic, conversion or both must move; sorting finds page-two, decayed, thin and mismatched posts.

steps.name: Fix titles, descriptions and sign-up prompts first
steps.why: Cheapest changes on pages that already get impressions and clicks.

steps.name: Refresh or write only the pages with sign-up potential
steps.why: A part-time writer cannot cover everything; real new value beats a changed date.

steps.name: Publish in batches and read against unchanged pages
steps.why: Results lag by weeks; unchanged pages show what the season did.

steps.name: Build links to the new pages
steps.why: Links lift rankings for competitive terms.

pitfalls.text: Changing the date on a post without adding real content; Google warns against this and Ahrefs says it can be ignored.
Writing many new posts for traffic that never signs up, instead of pages close to the product.
Trusting a GA4 sign-up count that is not set up as a key event or loses organic attribution.
Calling a result after a few days; indexing and ranking changes take days to months, so early reads mislead.
Counting position or traffic changes as caused by the edit when unchanged pages moved the same way.

hypotheses.statement: The baseline of about 15 organic sign-ups is wrong because tracking is incomplete or mis-attributed.
hypotheses.test: Compare GA4 organic sign-up key events with the product's real sign-up counts by month and check the event setup.
hypotheses.confirm_if: GA4 and the product differ by more than 15%, or the event is not a key event.
hypotheses.refute_if: The two agree within 15% and the event is a key event.

hypotheses.statement: Visitors do not reach a sign-up because most posts have no clear prompt.
hypotheses.test: For the top 10 posts by organic sessions, sign-ups per session and whether a prompt is visible.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Most of the top 10 convert below the 1.25% site average (15 of about 1,200) or have no prompt.
hypotheses.refute_if: The top posts already convert at 2% or better with a visible prompt.

hypotheses.statement: Many relevant queries sit on page two, so small improvements move clicks.
hypotheses.test: Count non-brand queries by page at positions 11 to 20 with at least 100 impressions in the window.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least 20 such queries across at least 5 posts.

hypotheses.statement: Posts that rank on page one lose clicks to weak titles and descriptions.
hypotheses.test: For queries at positions 1 to 5 with at least 100 impressions, compare click-through with the site median for the same position band.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least 5 pages sit 30% or more below the median for their band.
hypotheses.refute_if: Click-through is at or above the median.

hypotheses.statement: The 45 posts cover topics that bring readers who will not buy HR software.
hypotheses.test: Score each post's main query for business potential on a 0 to 3 scale and sum clicks by score.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than half of organic clicks go to posts scoring 0 or 1.
hypotheses.refute_if: More than half of clicks go to posts scoring 2 or 3.

hypotheses.statement: Several useful posts have lost traffic and can be recovered with a real refresh.
hypotheses.test: Compare clicks for the last 6 months with the 6 months before, and check for a content or link problem.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least 8 posts lost 30% or more of clicks and score 2 or 3 on business potential.
hypotheses.refute_if: Fewer than 3 do, or the losses are explained by falling demand.

hypotheses.statement: Some posts are not indexed or compete with each other for the same query.
hypotheses.test: Search Console indexing status per post, and queries where two or more posts each hold impressions.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least 10% of posts are not indexed, or at least 5 queries split impressions across two or more posts.
hypotheses.refute_if: All posts are indexed and fewer than 3 queries overlap.

hypotheses.statement: Many posts are thin or generic against Google's people-first checks.
hypotheses.test: Score each post on original information, visible authorship, sourcing and first-hand detail from Google's self-assessment themes.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least a third of posts fail three or more of those checks.
hypotheses.refute_if: Fewer than 10% fail three or more.

dropped.reason: The owner has no budget for links; the plan relies on page quality, internal links and rank improvements instead.

measurement.window: Read each change over at least 28 days after against the same 28 days before and against unchanged control pages; first read about six weeks after the first publish; verdict on the 100 a month target at month six.
measurement.min_volume: A page-level verdict needs at least 100 clicks in the before window or the pages are pooled; a sign-up verdict needs at least 30 organic sign-ups in the compared window, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.
measurement.stop_rule: Pause a change and ask the head of marketing if clicks to a changed page fall more than 10% against its control after 28 days, or a claim problem is found; otherwise keep the batch live for the full window.
